Message from the Chancellor 
Dear Students, 
It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to SR University. 
Your enthusiasm and energy bring vibrancy to our campus 
community. At SR University, we are reimagining education 
through innovative practices, aiming to create a dynamic 
ecosystem that nurtures holistic development. 
As you embark on this exciting journey, we look forward to 
growing, exploring, and learning together. Our university values 
academic excellence, diversity, and a spirit of inquiry. Here, you'll 
find a culture that encourages curiosity, critical thinking, a nd 
collaboration. You will have the opportunity to work alongside 
distinguished faculty on groundbreaking research and creative 
projects, while also gaining fresh perspectives through 
interaction with your talented peers.

We are committed to providing a rich, inclusive learning environment where every student is 
empowered to reach their full potential. As you begin this transformative phase, know that we are 
deeply invested in your growth and success.

Welcome to SRU. We wish you a fulfilling and inspiring educational experience. 
Warm regards, 
Varada Reddy Anagandula 
Chancellor, SR University

Vice-Chancellor – Prof. Deepak Garg 
Prof. Deepak Garg holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science, with a specialization in Efficient Algorithm 
Design, and brings over 26 years of academic leadership and research experience. He has previously 
served as Professor and Dean at Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology and Bennett University. 
Widely recognized as a leading voice in Artificial Intelligence in India, Prof. Garg writes a regular 
column titled "Breaking Shackles" in The Times of India, addressing higher education and AI trends. 
He has been an advisor to prestigious bodies such as A IRAWAT (Govt. of India’s Supercomputing 
Mission), NAAC, NBA, UGC, and AICTE. 
A passionate advocate for innovation and entrepreneurship, Prof. Garg actively mentors startups and 
serves on advisory boards of Drishya AI, ByteXL, and Global AI Hub. He is the only CAC ABET 
Commissioner from India and has been a Program Evaluator (PEV) for over seven years. 
He has served on the Board of Governors of the IEEE Education Society (USA) and chaired several IEEE 
bodies in India. With over 180 research publications, 2600+ citations, and an h -index of 22, his work 
spans Reinforcement Learning and Generative AI. He ha s mentored 14 Ph.D. scholars and led 
prestigious collaborations with over 100 global universities and industries. 
Prof. Garg also served as Director of the NVIDIA-Bennett Research Center on AI and led leadingindia.ai, 
India’s largest AI skilling initiative, impacting over a million students. He has delivered 350+ invited 
talks and keynotes across the country. His vision is to position SR University as a national benchmark 
for excellence in private higher education.

Welcome to SR University 
Congratulations on becoming a part of SR University. 
Student Handbook Purpose 
This Student Handbook serves as a comprehensive guide to academic regulations, student services, 
campus facilities, policies, and opportunities available at SR University 
1. ABOUT SR UNIVERSITY 
SR University (SRU) is a State Private University located in Warangal, Telangana. Spread across a 170-
acre verdant campus, the university is home to over 11,000 students and more than 1,200 faculty and 
staff, with six distinct schools. 
Vision 
• To accelerate the transformation and advancement of the regional innovation ecosystem 
through academic excellence, industry relevance, and social responsibility. 
Mission 
• Develop technically competent, industry-ready, and socially responsible leaders. 
• Undertake groundbreaking research and actively disseminate its outcomes. 
• Foster collaborations with industry, government, and non -profit organizations to serve the 
broader community. 
1.1 University Profile 
Rankings and Accreditations 
NIRF Rankings:  SRU is one of the youngest universities in India to achieve national recognition. It 
ranked 91st in Engineering in the year 2025. In the University category, it is placed in the 101–150 rank 
band. 
Academic Schools 
SR University offers a comprehensive range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs 
across the

following six academic schools: 
School of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence 
School of Engineering 
School of Business 
School of Agriculture 
School of Sciences and Humanities 
School of Design 
We encourage you to explore the University website  (https://sru.edu.in/) for detailed information 
about each school, including faculty, programs, and research initiatives. 
Research and Innovation Centers 
SRU is committed to multidisciplinary research and innovation through its state -of-the-art centers. 
These centers serve as collaborative spaces where students and faculty engage with real -world 
challenges and cutting-edge technologies: 
Nest for Entrepreneurship in Science & Technology (NEST) 
Center for Creative Cognition (CCC) 
Center for Design (CoD) 
Center for Embedded Systems & IoT (CEIoT) 
Center for AI & Deep Learning (CAIDL) 
Collaboratory for Social Innovation (CSI) 
Center for Materials & Manufacturing (CMM) 
Center for Emerging Energy Technologies (CEET) 
Center for Construction Methods & Materials (CCMM) 
Center for Experiential Learning (CEL) 
Centre for Nanomaterials (CNM) 
Center for Informetrics & Statistics (CIS) 
Visit the SRU website  (https://sru.edu.in/Research-Spotlite) to learn more about ongoing research 
projects, industry collaborations, innovation ecosystems, and upcoming events hosted by these

centers. They form the backbone of SRU’s mission to foster vibrant research and entrepreneurial 
culture. 
Sri Ranganatha Swamy Temple 
Located at the main entrance of the university, the Ranganatha Swamy Temple is a serene place of 
worship dedicated to Lord Ranganatha. With its traditional architecture and peaceful ambiance, the

temple serves as a spiritual landmark, offering students and faculty a space for reflection and devotion 
amidst their academic journeys. 
1.2. Administrative Offices and Student Support 
Office of Dean Student Welfare 
The Office of the Dean of Student Welfare oversees student welfare, campus engagement, hostel

administration, and student support services. The office works closely with students, faculty, the 
Student Council, and University leadership to ensure a supportive and enriching campus environment. 
Students may contact the office at dean.sw@sru.edu.in for assistance and guidance. 
Student Help Desk

The Student Help Desk serves as the primary contact point for student support and administrative 
assistance. It is located in Block-I, Room No. 1002 (Administrative Office) and functions on all working 
days up to 5:00 PM. Students are advised to contact the appropriate staff members as per the nature

of their request and follow the prescribed University procedures for timely resolution of issues.

1.3. Transportation Services 
SR University offers reliable and efficient transport services for day scholars from Monday to Friday. 
These services cover Kazipet, Hanamkonda, Warangal, and nearby districts such as Karimnagar, 
Husnabad, Jammikunta, and Huzurabad. 
Registration for Transportation Facility

Students who wish to avail of the university transport service must register with  Mr. B. Ramesh , 
Location: Block-I, Room No. 1002. 
Transportation Charges 
Transport services are chargeable, and the fee must be paid in full at the beginning of the academic 
year. The transport fee varies depending on the distance and specific stop location. No refunds will be

issued for partial or unused transport services. 
Bus Boarding Rules 
Students must board only at their registered stop; changing boarding points is not permitted. 
Personal Vehicle Policy 
Personal vehicles of the students are not allowed inside the campus. They must be parked outside the 
second gate at the designated space at the student’s own risk. The university will not be responsible

for any damage or theft of the vehicle. Cycles are al lowed inside the campus, and students can keep 
their cycles in the hostel.

2. STUDENT SUPPORT, ENGAGEMENT AND CAMPUS LIFE 
2.1. Student Registration and University Identity 
Enrollment Number Framework 
Enrollment and registration mark the formal commencement of a student’s academic journey at the 
University. The process, from admission to final enrollment, is structured to ensure transparency, 
accuracy, and systematic academic record management, as illustrated in Flowchart 1.1. 
Upon successful admission, a student’s enrollment remains provisional until the University officially 
assigns a unique Institutional Enrollment Number. To ensure administrative accuracy and avoid 
duplication of records, the University follows a structured enrollment identification framework. 
Each student is allotted a unique 10 -digit Enrollment Number representing the Year of Admission, 
School Code, Degree Code, Program Code, and serial number.  
Component Description 
Year of Admission Admission Year 
School Code School Identifier 
Degree Code Degree Type 
Program Code Program Identifier 
Serial Number Unique Student Number 
Example: For B. Tech CSE 
2 3 0 3 A 5 1 0 0 1 
Year of Admission School Code Degree Code Program Code Serial Number 
University Identification Card 
Every student shall be issued a University Identification Card containing the Enrollment Number, 
student photograph, name, and other essential details. The ID card serves as the official identity

credential within the University campus. 
Students are required to carry and wear the ID card at all times while on campus and during 
participation in external academic, sports, cultural, or official University activities. 
In case of loss or damage, a duplicate ID card may be issued upon payment of the prescribed fee as 
per University policy. 
2.2. Academic Working Hours and Campus Dress Code 
Institution and Transportation Timings 
Institute Timings for all UG, PG and PhD Courses: 9.00 A.M. to 5.00 P.M. 
Transportation Timings for Day-scholars: Arrival - 8.50 A.M. Departure - 5.05 P .M. 
Dress Code Policy 
Students are expected to maintain appropriate and professional attire while on campus. Clothing 
containing offensive language, inappropriate content, or excessively torn designs is discouraged 
within the University premises. 
Students should wear formal dress every Monday and Tuesday. In addition, formal attire is mandatory 
during technical presentations, seminars, meetings, placement activities, and all official University 
events conducted on any working day. 
Formal Dress Guidelines 
For Male Students 
Shirt: Collared formal shirt with full or half sleeves. 
Trousers: Plain formal trousers. Jeans, cargo pants, and shorts are not permitted. 
Footwear: Formal shoes are mandatory. Slippers, sandals, and casual footwear are not permitted. 
Professional Attire: Tie and blazer are recommended during presentations, seminars, placement 
activities, and formal University events. 
For Female Students 
Salwar Kameez: Neat and modest attire with dupatta. 
Kurti with Leggings/Churidar: Should be formal and appropriate in design and length. 
Saree/Formal Western Wear: Professional and modest attire suitable for academic and official

activities. 
Footwear: Closed-toe sandals or formal shoes are permitted. Slippers and flip-flops are not permitted. 
2.3. Academic and Administrative Digital Services (SRAAP) 
The SR Academic and Administration Portal (SRAAP) is the University's integrated digital platform for 
managing academic and administrative services. It provides students with seamless access to 
essential information and services throughout their academic journey. 
Key Features: Student Profile Management, Course Registration and Enrollment, Attendance 
Monitoring, Academic Performance Tracking, Examination Fee Payment, Academic Calendar and 
Regulations, Holiday Notifications, Faculty Feedback Submission, Grievance Redressal, Stude nt 
Engagement and Gamification Modules. SRAAP also facilitates communication with parents through 
periodic updates on attendance and academic performance, promoting transparency and student 
support. 
Login Credentials: 
Students will receive their login credentials during the registration or induction process. These 
credentials provide access to all services available on the portal. 
Support Contact: Mr. D. Kishore, sraap@sru.edu.in 
2.4. Mentoring and Academic Advising Framework 
The University recognizes mentoring and academic advising as integral components of student 
success, academic progression, and holistic development. Each student is assigned a faculty mentor

at 
the time of enrollment to provide continuous academic guidance and institutional support throughout 
the program. 
Mentoring System 
The mentoring framework is designed to support students in their academic, personal, and 
professional development. Faculty mentors act as the primary point of contact for guidance, support, 
and student engagement. 
Mentor Responsibilities 
Support students in academic and personal development. 
Facilitate timely communication and academic updates. 
Guide students in addressing academic challenges and identifying growth opportunities. 
Promote student engagement and overall well-being. 
Mentoring Engagement 
At least one individual mentor–mentee interaction shall be conducted each semester. 
At least one group mentoring session shall be organized each semester. 
Students are encouraged to seek guidance from their mentors whenever required. 
Academic Advising 
Academic advising complements the mentoring process by helping students make informed 
decisions regarding their academic progression and future career pathways. 
Academic Advising Areas 
Course Registration and Academic Planning. 
Goal Setting and Academic Progress Monitoring. 
Internships, Research, and Experiential Learning Opportunities. 
Higher Education and Career Development Pathways. 
Through mentoring and academic advising, students are supported in developing personalized 
learning pathways aligned with their academic interests, professional goals, and long-term aspirations.

2.5. Batch Representative System 
Each academic batch, comprising approximately 30 students, is represented by a Batch Representative 
(BR) selected at the start of every semester. The BR acts as the voice of their batch, presenting views, 
concerns, and grievances in meetings with the Dean, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, or Vice-Chancellor, typically 
conducted in the third or fourth week of the semester. 
Batch Representative Selection Process 
i. Opening Nominations 
o Announced by the Dean Academics through the SRAAP portal. 
ii. Collecting Nominations 
o Interested students submit their nominations via SRAAP.

iii. Selection Process 
o Students of the respective batch choose their preferred candidate on SRAAP. 
iv. Declaration of Results 
o The student with the highest number of choices is declared the BR. 
o If no nominations are received, the Head of the Department (HoD) will devise an 
internal process to nominate a representative. 
2.6. Learning Management System (LMS)

The University utilizes Learning Management Systems (LMS) such as Google Classroom , or other 
approved digital learning platforms to support teaching, learning, and academic engagement. These 
platforms provide a centralized digital learning environment for course delivery and academic 
communication. 
• Course Content and Learning Resources 
• Assignments and Submission Portals

• Academic Announcements and Discussions 
• Assessments, Quizzes, and Feedback 
• Multimedia Learning Materials 
Students are required to access the LMS using their official University email credentials. The LMS 
platform adopted for a course shall be determined by the respective course instructor. Students are

expected to regularly access the LMS and actively participate in all prescribed learning activities. 
2.7. Student Feedback and Escalation Framework 
Open Door Policy 
The University follows a transparent and student-centric Open Door Policy that encourages students 
to share suggestions, concerns, and feedback regarding academic and campus -related matters.

Students may communicate with faculty members, administrative off ices, or University leadership 
through meetings, official emails, or scheduled appointments. Students are encouraged to follow the 
prescribed communication hierarchy for routine matters before approaching higher authorities. The 
University values construct ive feedback as an important component of continuous institutional

improvement and student engagement. 
Feedback Mechanism 
The Office of Dean Academics collects student feedback before Mid Sem and End Sem examinations 
through the University’s online feedback system. Students, parents, and alumni may also submit 
feedback and suggestions through the official communication channel at feedback@sru.edu.in. The

University remains committed to continuously improving the overall learning and campus experience 
through active stakeholder participation. 
Student Grievance Redressal Cell 
The Student Grievance Redressal Cell functions as the designated institutional mechanism for 
addressing student grievances and concerns related to academic, administrative, and campus matters.

Students may submit grievances through the official email ID stu.grievance@sru.edu.in or contact the 
University Help Desk. All grievances shall be reviewed and resolved within a reasonable timeframe 
based on the nature and severity of the issue.  
For any queries Contact: Mr. P. Naresh- 9989221167, p.nareshkumar@sru.edu.in 
2.8. Student Council

The University promotes student leadership, participation, and democratic representation through the 
Student Council framework. The Student Council functions as a structured platform for student 
engagement in academic, cultural, social, and co-curricular activities of the University. 
(Refer Flowchart 2.6 for Student Council Mechanism.) 
Council Structure

The University-level Student Council shall consist of the following office bearers: 
• President  
• Vice President  
• General Secretary

• Joint Secretary  
• Treasurer  
• Cultural Secretary  
Eligibility Criteria 
General Eligibility 
Students applying for Student Council positions shall: 
• Be bonafide students of the University  
• Have no active backlogs at the time of nomination  
• Minimum 75% attendance in the previous semester. 
• Maintain a minimum CGPA of 7 or equivalent  
• Have no disciplinary action or warning issued against them  
• Demonstrate active participation in departmental, club, cultural, or student engagement 
activities

Student Council nominations shall be invited through the prescribed online application process. 
Applicants shall submit:

All nominations shall be reviewed and scrutinized by the Office of Dean Student Welfare. 
Selection and Tenure 
The Student Council shall be constituted annually for a tenure

shortlisted eligible candidates. 
Roles and Responsibilities

General Secretary Maintains records and coordinates meetings and events

Cultural Secretary Coordinates cultural and student engagement activities 
Code of Conduct 
All Student Council members are expected to: 
• Maintain discipline and professional conduct  
• Attend meetings and assigned activities regularly

• Perform duties ethically, transparently, and inclusively  
• Avoid misuse of authority, position, or University resources  
• Follow all University rules and regulations  
Faculty Oversight 
The Dean Student Welfare and Associate Deans shall provide guidance, supervision, and administrative 
support for Student Council activities and meetings. 
Disqualification and Removal 
A Student Council member may be removed from office under the following circumstances: 
• Involvement in misconduct, indiscipline, or academic dishonesty  
• Continuous absence from official meetings without valid reason  
• Misuse of position, authority, or University resources  
• Violation of University rules, policies, or code of conduct

2.9 Student Clubs and Professional Societies 
Clubs at the university provide a platform for students to develop talents, explore interests, and 
pursue passions. Students are encouraged to join at least one club per semester to expand their skills 
and experiences. 
The clubs aim to identify and nurture students’ potential, supporting their academic and personal 
growth through engaging activities. Open to all, these clubs organize events year -round, enriching 
students’ social, cultural, and academic experiences. They serve as a hub for learning, networking, and 
socializing beyond the classroom. For more details on club activities, visit the university website. 
The following clubs are active for the academic year 2025-26 onwards. 
University Level Clubs: 
Garden Club:  The Garden Club is committed to restoring a sustainable ecosystem while fostering 
interest in horticulture, gardening, and garden therapy. It encourages the beautification of the college 
campus, inspiring students to take an active role in environmental conservation. Through floral design 
and greenery initiatives, the club cultivates a passion for gardening and promotes civic engagement in 
sustainable practices. 
Organic Farming Club: The Organic Farming Club is a student-led initiative that promotes sustainable 
agriculture and environmentally conscious practices within the university community. The

club serves 
as a platform for students, faculty, and staff who are passionate about orga nic cultivation, food 
security, and ecological balance. 
Yoga Club:  This club promotes confidence, enthusiasm, and well -being in a non -competitive 
environment. It enhances physical and emotional health, improves focus, concentration, and memory, 
and helps ease stress and anxiety. Through regular practice, students develop better posture, patience, 
and self-awareness, fostering relaxation, mindfulness, and inner balance. 
Literary Master Communicators Club:  This club enhances communication skills across diverse 
contexts, fostering critical thinking, confidence, and performance abilities for inter -collegiate events 
and contests. 
Artistic ( Painting and Sketching ) Club: This club nurtures creativity, confidence, and artistic 
exploration through various painting and sketching techniques. Students engage with historical and 
contemporary artistic practices, expanding their ideas and personal styles. By developing their own 
work, they cultivate self -expression, innovative thinking, and design skills, fostering a deeper 
appreciation for visual arts. 
Community Service Center: This center encourages students to identify community issues, engage in 
problem-solving, and develop a strong sense of civic responsibility. It fosters leadership, teamwork, 
and social awareness, helping

students apply their knowledge to real-world challenges. Through active 
participation, members gain skills in mobilizing community efforts, responding to emergencies, and 
promoting social harmony, contributing to national integration and collective well-being. 
Martial Arts Club:  The Martial Arts Club promotes fitness, self -confidence, and discipline through 
structured training. Members develop physical strength, mental resilience, and teamwork, while 
learning both defensive and offensive techniques in a safe and supportive environment. 
Adventure Club: This club offers students exciting opportunities to explore nature, build resilience, 
and develop leadership through activities like trekking, camping, and rock climbing. It encourages 
teamwork, eco-awareness, and personal growth beyond the classroom. 
Hiking Club: This club encourages students to explore local trails, stay active, and connect with nature. 
It promotes fitness, mindfulness, and outdoor camaraderie. 
Cultural Club:  The Cultural Club is dedicated to celebrating the diverse traditions and festivals 
observed across different communities. It serves as a platform for students to embrace cultural 
heritage through various events, performances, and interactive activities. The club organizes festivals,

traditional celebrations, and artistic showcases, promoting inclusivity and unity within the student 
body.  
Sports Club: The Sports Club fosters athletic skills, teamwork, and discipline while promoting physical 
fitness, mental resilience, and social awareness. It encourages sportsmanship, leadership, and 
cooperation through sports events, training, and competitions, helping students build confidence and 
teamwork. 
Drama and Theatre Club: This club fosters self-expression, confidence, and creativity through acting 
and performances. It enhances social interaction, imagination, and teamwork, helping students build 
confidence while making learning fun. 
Photography and Movie Making Club: This club encourages students to explore creativity in 
photography and video production, helping them develop a strong visual aesthetic through compiling, 
editing, and storytelling. It fosters technical, artistic, and perceptual skills, allowing students to express 
their ideas while discovering potential career opportunities. Members experiment with natural and 
artificial settings, refining their ability to manipulate and control artistic vision through engaging 
projects. 
Dance Club: This club that provides students with opportunities to learn and perform various dance 
forms and styles. The club offers training in different genres of dance, including contemporary, 
classical, folk,

western, and freestyle, while encouraging creativity and sel f-expression. Members 
actively participate in flash mobs, cultural events, and intercollegiate competitions, showcasing their

2.10. Campus Events and Student Engagement Activities 
The University is committed to holistic student development by fostering a vibrant campus life that 
balances academics with extracurricular activities. With a large residential student population, the 
university ensures a conducive environment where studen ts can grow both personally and 
professionally.

Freshers Party

and interactive activities, fostering friendships and easing their transition into university life. The 
Fresher’s Party is held in first month after start of 1st year classes.

at the start of each semester. It provides a platform for students to explore various clubs —ranging 
from cultural, technical and social —enhancing leaders hip, creativity, and engagement within and 
outside the campus. 
Independence Day

hoisting ceremonies, speeches, and cultural performances. Celebrated annually on August 15th, it 
instils a deep sense of pride and national responsibility among students.

together for traditional floral arrangements, folk music, and dances. Held in September or October as

calendar, this event show cases various traditions, fosters academic exchanges, and promotes 
intercultural understanding among students.

hosts formal events, including student -led parades, discussions on civic duties, and cultural 
showcases, reinforcing the values of democracy and citizenship.

in a range of athletic competitions and recreational activities. Typically organized in February or 
March, it

campus.

3. ACADEMIC REGULATIONS AND ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK  
3.1. Academic Definitions and Terminology 
Term Definition 
Academic Calendar A semester schedule outlining teaching periods, exams, holidays, 
deadlines, and events. Accessible via SRAAP. 
Academic Council The highest academic authority overseeing instruction, research, and 
evaluation. Includes the VC, Deans, HoDs, faculty representatives, and 
external experts. 
Academic Year Spans July to June, comprising Odd and Even semesters, plus Summer 
Semester for backlog/improvement courses.

Board of Studies (BoS) Department-level academic body responsible for designing and updating 
syllabi, chaired by the Head of department and including departmental 
faculty and external experts. 
Capstone Project A final-year credit-based project reflecting cumulative program learning 
under faculty mentorship. 
CGPA (Cumulative 
Grade Point Average) 
Overall academic performance across all semesters, calculated as the 
total credit-weighted grade points divided by total credits. 
Degree with 
Specialization 
Awarded upon successful completion of core program courses and a 
defined set of specialization courses.

3.3. International Mobility and Global Learning Opportunities 
The University provides multiple international learning pathways and global

academic engagement 
opportunities through collaborations with reputed international institutions. These programs are 
coordinated through the Office of International Affairs and Corporate Outreach (IACO). 
Semester Abroad Program 
Eligible students may apply to study for one semester at partner universities abroad based on the 
guidelines and selection criteria prescribed by IACO. Students participating in the program shall pay 
the applicable University tuition fee along with the prescribed international program charges. 
Summer Immersion Program 
The University facilitates short-term international immersion programs ranging from 1 to 6 weeks at 
globally recognized institutions such as NUS, FPT University, and San Francisco State University. 
These programs are intended to provide global academic exposure, interdisciplinary learning, and 
cultural experience. 
Subject to the duration, structure, and academic content of the immersion program, students may 
be permitted to claim eligible open elective or professional elective credits with prior approval from 
the University. 
International Business Accelerated Program (IBAP) 
Under the IBAP pathway, students complete three years of study at the University under the BBA 
program and may pursue advanced studies for two additional years at partner institutions in the 
USA, such as UMass Lowell, leading to an MBA or MS degree in

Finance or Business Analytics. 
International Engineering Program (IEP) 
The University offers multiple international engineering pathways in collaboration with foreign 
universities: 
• 2+2 Model: Two years at the University followed by two years abroad leading to an 
undergraduate degree.  
• 3+1+1 Model: Three years at the University, one year abroad for undergraduate completion, 
and an optional additional year for a master’s degree.  
Progression Pathway Programs 
The University also facilitates progression-based international programs through academic 
partnerships with foreign universities. Under these pathways, students may transfer during the final 
phase of their undergraduate program to pursue integrated bachelor’s and master’s degree

opportunities abroad. Eligibility criteria and admission requirements shall be governed by the 
respective partner institution policies. 
For further details regarding international programs and global academic pathways, students may 
contact the Office of International Affairs and Corporate Outreach (IACO). 
3.4. Honours and Minor Degree Framework 
Honours Degree 
The Honours Degree framework enables academically motivated students to pursue advanced 
learning in their discipline through additional specialized coursework. 
• Students must maintain the prescribed minimum CGPA at the time of registration and award 
of the Honours Degree.  
• A minimum of 16 credits shall be earned through approved advanced courses.  
• These credits must be completed through overloading during regular or Summer Semesters.  
• Courses completed under the Honours framework shall not overlap with the core curriculum 
requirements of the parent program.  
• Additional registration fees shall apply as per University policy.  
• These courses can be also taken in summer semester. 
Minor Degree 
The Minor Degree framework provides students the opportunity to acquire multidisciplinary 
knowledge in a secondary domain outside their parent discipline. 
• Students shall complete a minimum of 16 credits from an approved Minor course basket.  
• Registration through course overloading is mandatory.  
•

Minor courses shall be distinct from the core curriculum of the parent program.  
• Additional fees shall be applicable for the registered Minor courses as per university policy. 
• These courses can be also taken in summer semester.

3.8. Grading System and Academic Performance Evaluation 
The University follows a grading system for evaluating student performance in each course. Letter 
grades are awarded based on a student’s academic performance as per the overall performance of 
the course cohort to ensure fairness, consistency, and academic rigor. Each letter grade is associated 
with a corresponding Grade Point (GP), which is used for the computation of the Semester Grade Point

average of grade points earned in all courses registered during a semester, while the CGPA reflects 
the cumulative academic performance across all completed semesters of the program. The de tailed 
grading framework, grade points, and methodology for SGPA and CGPA computation are provided in

3.9. Examination Process, Academic Recovery and Grade Improvement Framework 
The University adopts a comprehensive assessment framework designed to evaluate student learning, 
competency development, analytical ability, and academic progression through a combination of 
Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) and End Semester Examination (ESE).

Examination Eligibility 
Students shall be eligible to appear for any examination only if they: 
Are registered for the course; 
Have completed the prescribed examination registration process; 
Have paid the applicable examination fee; and 
Fulfil the minimum attendance requirements prescribed by the University. 
Failure to satisfy these requirements may result in withholding examination eligibility and award of an 
appropriate grade as per University regulations. 
Closed Book and Open Book Examinations 
The University may conduct examinations in either Closed Book or Open Book mode depending on 
the nature of the course and the intended learning outcomes. 
Closed Book Examination 
A Closed Book Examination assesses students without access to textbooks, notes, or reference 
material and primarily evaluates conceptual understanding, retention, and problem-solving ability. 
Open Book Examination 
An Open Book Examination permits students to refer to approved learning resources during the 
examination. Such examinations are designed to evaluate application of knowledge, critical thinking, 
analysis, interpretation, and problem-solving rather than memorization. 
The mode of examination shall be determined by the University from time to time and notified 
through the approved examination schedule. 
Assessment and Evaluation 
Each course shall be coordinated by a designated Course

Coordinator responsible for assessment 
planning, evaluation, and grade submission. Continuous Internal Evaluation may include one or more 
of the following components: 
Mid-Term Examinations 
Quizzes and Class Tests 
Assignments and Case Studies 
Laboratory Evaluation and Viva Voce 
Presentations and Seminars 
Projects and Design Challenges 
Hackathons and Innovation Activities 
Industry Certifications and Experiential Learning Activities 
Internships, Capstone Projects, Industry Projects, and other experiential learning components shall be 
evaluated through approved evaluation committees constituted by the University. 
Final grades shall be awarded based on overall performance in Continuous Internal Evaluation and 
End Semester Examination as per the approved grading framework. 
Review and Re-evaluation of Answer Scripts 
To promote transparency and academic accountability, students shall be provided an opportunity to 
review evaluated answer scripts within the schedule notified by the concerned department. Students 
who identify discrepancies in evaluation may seek clarification from the course instructor during the 
review process. Any correction arising out of evaluation oversight may be incorporated before final 
grade submission. Students who do not attend the answer script review session within the notified 
schedule shall forfeit their right to review the answer script. However, students may subsequently 
apply for re-evaluation by paying the prescribed fee. 
Following the declaration of results, students may apply for re-evaluation of answer scripts under the 
following circumstances: 
Missed Review:  The student was unable to attend the scheduled answer script review session 
conducted by the faculty. 
Dissatisfaction After Review: The student attended the review session but remains dissatisfied with 
the evaluation of the answer script. 
Applications for re-evaluation shall be submitted within the timeline prescribed by the Examination

Branch along with the applicable fee. The outcome of the re -evaluation process shall be final and 
binding. 
Mid-Term Make-up Examination 
Students who are absent for the Mid-Term Examination or secure less than the prescribed qualifying 
marks may register for a Mid -Term Make-up Examination by paying the prescribed fee within the 
notified schedule. The marks secured in the Mid-Term Make-up Examination shall replace the original 
Mid-Term marks for evaluation purposes. 
Scaling End term marks by adding additional marks in proportion to midterm total marks. 
To provide an additional opportunity for academic improvement, students who are not satisfied with 
their Mid -Term Make -up Examination performance may apply for proportionate scaling of End 
Semester Examination marks towards Mid-Term marks by paying the prescribed fee. 
The scaled Mid -Term marks shall be computed based on the student's performance in the End 
Semester Examination and the approved evaluation weightages of the course. 
The final Mid-Term marks shall be the higher of Mid-Term Make-up Examination Marks or Scaled Mid-
Term Marks. 
The detailed computation methodology shall be notified by the Controller of Examinations from time 
to time  and implemented as per the University policy. The scaling process shall not reduce the 
student's existing Mid-Term score.

Grade Improvement Policy 
Students awarded grades A, B+, B, or C may register for Grade Improvement subject to the following 
conditions: 
Grade Improvement shall be permitted only before graduation. 
Registration shall be completed within the schedule notified by the Examination Branch. 
Only one Grade Improvement attempt shall be permitted per course. 
Students shall undergo all evaluation components of the course irrespective of previous attempts. 
The better of the two grades shall be retained for CGPA computation. 
Revised grades shall be considered for academic progression, internships, placements, international 
mobility, and eligibility for Honors or Minor programs. 
Revised grades shall not be considered for award of university medals or ranks. 
Academic Recovery Framework 
The University provides structured academic recovery mechanisms to support student progression 
and successful completion of academic requirements. 
Clearing Not Registered Courses 
Courses not registered during the prescribed registration period shall be treated as Not Registered 
Courses. Students may complete such courses during subsequent regular semesters or Summer 
Semesters subject to: 
Availability of the course; 
Timetable feasibility;

Approval of the concerned academic authorities; and 
Payment of the prescribed fee. 
In case of semester withdrawal or semester drop, students shall comply with the applicable fee and 
registration requirements prescribed by the University. 
Clearing F Grade 
Students awarded an F grade may appear for the immediate Supplementary Examination. 
Only one supplementary attempt shall be permitted. 
The Supplementary Examination shall normally be conducted for 100 marks. 
The maximum grade that may be awarded through Supplementary Examination shall be C. 
Clearing R Grade 
Students awarded an R grade shall re -register for the course and complete all prescribed evaluation 
components. 
Such courses may be completed through the immediate or subsequent Summer Semester or 
whenever the course is next offered. 
Clearing I Grade 
Students awarded an I grade may appear for the End Semester Make-up Examination after completing 
the prescribed registration process and payment of the applicable fee. 
The Make-up Examination marks shall replace the End Semester Examination marks. 
Original course grading criteria and grade cut-offs shall be applicable. 
The Make-up Examination shall normally be conducted for 100 marks and scaled appropriately to the 
End Semester Examination weightage of the course. 
Failure to utilize the Make -up Examination opportunity shall result in the course being

treated as a 
failed course. 
Clearing MOOCs Courses 
Students who fail a MOOCs course may: 
Re-register for the same MOOCs course during a subsequent offering; or 
Register for an approved equivalent course with prior approval of the concerned academic authorities.

To facilitate timely graduation, the University may conduct Advance Supplementary Examinations for

Declaration of Results

universities, academic institutions, research organizations, and approved learning platforms in India

3.17. Degree Award Requirements and Academic Honors 
Eligibility for Award of Degree 
The University recognizes academic excellence by awarding degrees and honors to students who meet 
the required criteria. These awards motivate students to maintain high academic standards and overall 
discipline. 
A student is eligible for the award of a degree upon fulfilling the following conditions: 
Minimum CGPA for UG: 6.00 or above. 
Completion of All Courses and Compliance of all academic rules and regulations. 
Clearance of Dues: Payment of all fees with no pending disciplinary cases.

Academic Honors and Medals 
The University shall award Gold Medals in all UG/ PG/ diploma Programs. The Gold Medal shall be 
awarded only to students who have successfully completed the respective programs of study and are 
merited for such an award as per the criteria laid below. 
Chancellor’s Gold Medal 
Awarded to the best one UG student based on academic performance across all programs and 
branches in the University, provided there are a minimum number of students in the program. It will 
be based on the final CGPA of the student. The student should not have backlogs throughout the 
program and should not have any disciplinary case. Minimum eligibility for Chancellor’s Gold Medal is 
9.0 CGPA. 
Vice-Chancellor’s Medal 
Awarded to the top-performing students in order of Gold Medal/Silver Medal/Bronze Medal in each 
program/branch of the university. The student should not have backlogs throughout the program and 
should not have any disciplinary case. Minimum eligibility for Vice-Chancellor’s Medal is 8.5 CGPA. 
Semester Topper Award 
The Semester Topper Award is presented to the student with the highest performance in gamification 
points including academics in each semester. Minimum eligibility for Semester Topper Award is 8.0 
CGPA. 
Award Criteria- One topper per batch per program each semester. 
Tie-Breaking Rules 
Student Success Management points as per the SRAAP dashboard.  
Highest number of A, B grades (in that order). 
If still tied, the younger student (as per Date of Birth) will be awarded.

4. STUDENT CONDUCT, DISCIPLINE AND GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL 
4.1.  Student Code of Conduct 
The University is committed to fostering a culture rooted in responsibility, inclusivity, and academic 
integrity. The university encourages students to embrace the freedom of learning while upholding 
ethical behaviour, mutual respect, and social accountability. The follo wing Code of Conduct outlines 
the expected standards of behaviour for all students across academic, digital, and social domains. 
Applicability of the Code 
The code shall be applicable to all students admitted to the university and including any academic 
program, activity or event conducted by the university. It is the duty and responsibility of each student 
from the date of admission to get acquainted with all the rules and code of conduct. All students are 
required to strictly adhere to this code and this code would be binding on and enforceable on them. 
Student Responsibilities 
It shall be the responsibility of the student, 
To produce Identity Card whenever asked by any official/staff of the university. 
To foster and maintain a vibrant academic, intellectual, cultural and social atmosphere which is 
consistent with the objectives of the university. 
To access all educational opportunities and benefits available at the university and make good use of 
them to prosper academically. 
To respect the laws of the country, human rights and to always conduct in a responsible and dignified 
manner. To report any violation of this code to the functionaries of the university. 
Student joining in any academic program of the university will have to give an undertaking to the effect 
that the student will comply with the provisions envisaged in this code in letter and spirit and even if 
it is not given, they will be bound by the provisions of this code. 
General Conduct Expectations 
Respect and Inclusivity: Students shall embrace diversity and uphold mutual respect, regardless of 
background, culture, or belief. 
Personal Appearance and Behaviour: Maintain decency in attire and uphold decorum in all university

spaces, both physical and digital. 
Civic Responsibility: Always demonstrate courtesy and consideration toward faculty, staff, peers, and 
the campus community. 
Social Media Use: Posting defamatory or inappropriate content, including reels or images against the 
university or its members, is prohibited and subject to disciplinary action. 
Digital Citizenship: Students are expected to use university -provided digital platforms ethically and 
refrain from creating unauthorized groups or sharing misleading content. 
SRU discourages the use of single-use plastics on campus to support environmental sustainability. 
4.2. Academic Integrity and Ethical Conduct 
Students must uphold the highest standards of honesty and responsibility in academic pursuits. 
Academic dishonesty undermines the core values of SRU and will not be tolerated. 
All submissions, assessments, and research must be the student’s own. Collaborative work is 
permitted only when explicitly authorized. 
Plagiarism: Students must properly acknowledge all external ideas, images, data, and digital content, 
including content generated by AI tools. 
Cheating and Fabrication: Use of unauthorized aids, impersonation, falsifying records, or tampering 
with academic documents is prohibited. 
Respect for Evaluation Processes: Attempting to influence grading decisions or disrupting others' 
academic work is unethical and

subject to penalty. 
Discipline and Prohibited Conduct 
Substance Abuse: SRU enforces a strict zero-tolerance policy toward alcohol, drugs, tobacco, and any 
other prohibited substances on campus. 
Harassment and Discrimination: Any form of harassment —verbal, physical, emotional, sexual, or 
cyber is forbidden. 
Possession of Weapons: Carrying weapons or dangerous items on campus is strictly prohibited. 
Dress and Identification: Students are expected to wear formal  attire on Monday and Tuesday or 
decent attire during academic hours and must always carry their university ID card. 
Mobile Phone Policy 
Permitted Use: Mobile phones must be used responsibly. 
Prohibited Areas: Usage is banned in classrooms, laboratories, and examination halls. 
Misuse: Use of mobile phones for recording or sharing unauthorized content may result in confiscation 
and disciplinary measures. 
Banned Content: Accessing or distributing offensive, pornographic, or illegal material using university 
networks is punishable. 
Disciplinary Measures and Consequences 
Violations of the Code of Conduct may lead to one or more of the following. 
Formal warning or reprimand. 
Suspension from specific classes, hostels, or activities. 
Cancellation of examinations or assignments. 
Financial penalties. 
Rustication or permanent expulsion. 
Withdrawal of scholarships or other academic privileges. 
All decisions will be made by the Disciplinary Committee based on the nature and gravity of the 
offense. 
Research and Publication Ethics 
Students engaged in research are expected to adhere to international standards of academic ethics. 
Responsible Research: Ensure ethical treatment of human and animal subjects and responsible 
disposal of research materials.

Publishing Guidelines 
Avoid duplicate submissions or simultaneous submissions to multiple journals.

Limit conference submissions to maximum three papers per event. 
Do not list non-contributing authors or use non SRU affiliations without formal approval. 
Fabrication of data or plagiarism in research is prohibited. 
University reserves the right to amend the Code of Conduct periodically. All students are required to 
stay informed via official communication channels. 
Security

The safety and security of the students on campus is of utmost priority to the university. Security 
guards are deployed round the clock across all the academic blocks, hostels, all exit points and key 
areas. These areas are also under 24x7 monitoring through CCTV cameras. 
All the hostel students must not leave the campus without completing the out -pass process. The

students entering the campus are physically frisked and their belongings are checked every time by 
the security guards to prevent carrying prohibited items into the hostels.

4.4. Punishment Provisions in cases of Ragging 
Any student or group of students found guilty of ragging on campus or off campus shall be liable to 
one or more of the following punishments:  
Debarring from appearing in any mid exam/ university examination or withholding results. 
Suspension from attending classes and academic privileges. 
Withdrawing scholarships and other benefits. 
Suspension from the college for a period of one month. 
Cancellation of admission. 
Debarring from representing the institution in any national or international meet, tournament, youth 
festival, etc. 
Suspension/expulsion from the hostel. 
Rustication from the institution for periods varying from 1 to 4 semesters or equivalent period. 
Expulsion from the institution and consequent debarring from admission to any other institution. 
Fine ranging between Rs. 25,000/- and Rupees 1 Lakh.  
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to ten 
thousand rupees or with

both. 
Collective punishment - When the students committing or abetting the crime of ragging are not 
identified, the institution shall resort to collective punishment as a deterrent to ensure community 
pressure on the potential raggers. 
4.5. Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) in Workplace 
University is committed to providing a safe and respectful environment for all members of its 
academic community, including staff and students. This Sexual Harassment Policy aims to prevent and 
address any form of sexual harassment within the university setting. It applies to all staff, students, 
and visitors and reflects our commitment to fostering a culture of respect, dignity, and inclusivity. 
Any student who experiences or witnesses sexual harassment is strongly encouraged to report the 
incident promptly to the appropriate authorities. Reporting can be done through multiple channels, 
including- Mentor, Head of the Department, Dean, and POSH Committee of the University. 
Reports can be made verbally or in writing and will be treated with confidentiality. The university is 
committed to conducting a thorough, impartial, and timely investigation of all complaints of sexual 
harassment. 
If an investigation confirms that sexual harassment has occurred, appropriate disciplinary action will 
be taken against the perpetrator, which may include but is not limited to, Counseling,

Formal warning, 
Suspension or Expulsion, and Legal consequences. 
University adheres to the POSH act of UGC, recognizing that sexual harassment is more prevalent 
among female staff and students, Regulation 3 (d) of the UGC POSH regulation mandates prompt 
action by Higher Educational University’s in the wake of any such harassment, the full regulations are 
available at https://7203627_UGC_regulations-harassment.pdf, SRU students and its staff members 
must adhere to these practices as mentioned thereof. 
The POSH Committee at SR University consists of Vice-Chancellor (Chairperson), two senior lady 
professors, Dean, Student Welfare, one woman faculty member from each department, and three girl 
students representing various academic levels.  
4.6. Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC) 
The University has constituted a Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC) to address student grievances, 
disciplinary concerns, and cases of misconduct in a fair and transparent manner. 
Based on the nature and severity of the issue, the concerned case may be referred to the GRC for 
detailed enquiry and resolution. The Committee shall examine the matter, recommend appropriate

corrective or disciplinary action, and submit its report to the Chairperson of the GRC within the 
prescribed timeline, normally within one week from the date of enquiry. 
Right to Appeal 
Students aggrieved by any decision or disciplinary action taken by an authority subordinate to the 
Associate Dean (Student Welfare) may submit an appeal to the Dean (Student Welfare). Appeals

against decisions of the Dean (Student Welfare) may be submitted to the Vice-Chancellor. 
All appeals shall be submitted within two weeks from the date of communication of the decision, along 
with proper justification and supporting documents, if any. The decision of the Vice -Chancellor shall

7.1 Attendance and Examination Policies  
Every student shall ordinarily attend all classes in a course. However, the minimum attendance in a 
prescribed course is 75%. The attendance shall be reckoned for theory and practical separately. A

student who fails to put in the minimum attendance either in theory or practical, his/her registration 
for that course shall be treated as cancelled. 
The minimum attendance requirements can be relaxed up to 10% on medical grounds i.e., up to 65% 
for theory and practical separately. 
As per ICAR Dean’s committee recommendations 85% attendance is required for student READY 
programmes. 
Evaluation and Results 
Evaluation of students, examinations and grades 
The evaluation of the student in a course shall be based on his /her performance in various kinds of 
examinations, records, class work and other types of exercises. 
The detailed course outlines in each course shall be prepared by the teacher(s) concerned  in 
consultation with the University Head of the Department/Head of the Department, which will be made 
available to the students during the first week of the semester. A schedule of the mid -semester 
examinations of the academic programme shall be prepared by the Dean and notified to the students 
at the beginning of each semester. 
Answer scripts of mid -semester examinations are evaluated by the teacher shall be shown to the 
students. The students shall have the option to request the teacher for clarification of any doubts in 
scoring, provided that such clarification is requested for when the answer scripts are made available 
to them. This shall not apply

forboth the final theory and practical examinations. 
Mid-semester examinations 
There shall be one mid-semester examination to be conducted by the teacher offering the course after 
50% of the working days are over in a semester. The duration for the mid-semester examination shall 
be for one and half hours and the final theory examination shall be two and half hours. 
The marks allotted for mid -semester and semester final theory examinations shall be 50 and 100, 
respectively. Ordinarily no condonation for absence of mid -semester examination shall be given. 
However, the mid semester examination to be conducted to the students who could not appear these 
examinations in view of their participation in the inter -University and National Sports, Literary and 
Cultural events etc., along with the students who genuinely prevented from taking examination in the 
case of serious illness or accident or any other case. This repeat examination shall be held within two 
weeks from the date of examinations so missed and  shall be a common examination for all such 
students. 
Unless a student appears for the mid-semester examination, he/she shall not be permitted to appear 
for the semester final theory and practical examinations in the course concerned. The special re -
examination shall be conducted as per the time to be fixed by the Dean within two weeks from the 
last date of mid

semester examinations. The weightage of marks  allotted for mid semester and 
semester final theory examination shall be as per VDeans Committee recommendations. 
Semester final examinations 
The final examinations shall be held at the end of each semester in each course. The final examination 
in the theory portion shall be of two and half hour’s duration. It shall be the responsibility of the 
University to conduct the theory portion of the final examination. Practical examinations shall be 
conducted by the respective colleges. The students shall be given two preparation holidays (including 
the public holiday) before the commencement of the semester final theory examinations. 
Answer scripts of semester final theory examinations are evaluated through common spot valuation 
system year of study wise. On the last day of semester final examinations, the Dean shall send all the 
sealed answer scripts to the selected center where they are coded, before distribution for valuation. 
The duration of the spot valuation is 7 (seven) working days. Evaluation instructions are issued by the 
University from time to time for each semester. 
Computation and award of courses grades

examination which shall include a viva -voce examination. In respect of RAWE Programme/ In plant

criteria for evaluation of students as prescribed in manuals of respective programmes shall be

ANNEXURE-I 
I. RESEARCH ETHICS 
SRU's Research Ethics Policy mandates trustworthiness and transparency in all research findings. All 
campuses utilize premium anti-plagiarism software, Turnitin/iThenticate. Researchers must adhere to 
UGC guidelines regarding plagiarism regulations and san ctions (refer to www.plagiarism.org for 
information on plagiarism and its consequences). SRU strongly discourages plagiarism in any form. 
Furthermore, the institution provides researchers with access to international state-of-the-art digital 
databases to e nsure research quality and the uniqueness of research questions and hypotheses. 
Necessary statistical analysis software is also provided to ensure data robustness and reliable results. 
All research students are required to maintain a detailed research note book documenting daily 
research activities. Each student stores their data in an immutable network folder, regularly examined 
and evaluated by the research guide. Intentional destruction or deletion of notebook or electronic 
folder information may result in disciplinary action. Similarly, any researcher found manipulating data 
will face severe consequences, including potential termination. 
Human Trials-Based Research and Other Related Policies 
SRU permits research involving human trials, and researchers must be aware of relevant Indian 
regulations, including The Drugs and

Cosmetics Act of 1940, the Medical Council of India Act of 1956, 
and the Central Council for Indian Medicine Act of 1970. Ini tiating a clinical trial in India necessitates 
the following: 
• Approval from the DCGI (Drugs Controller General of India). 
• Ethics Committee Approval in each country where the study is conducted. 
• Registration on the ICMR (Indian Council of Medical Research) website if the study involves cross-
border participation. 
Researchers should note the ICMR's evolving ethical guidelines: the 1980 Policy Statement on Ethical 
Considerations in Human Subjects Research, the 2000 Ethical Guidelines for Biomedical Research on 
Human Subjects (revised in 2006), and the recent ICMR Eth ical Guidelines for Biomedical and Health 
Research involving Human Participants. For clinical trials, the Central Drugs Standard Control 
Organization (CDSCO) published the Indian Good Clinical Practice Guidelines (2001) in 2005 and 
amended the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules in 2013. Guidelines for Stem Cell Research and Therapy were 
initially published in 2007 by the ICMR and the Department of Biotechnology (DBT). SRU and its 
researchers are required to follow all ethical guidelines provided in the most current ICMR Ethical 
Guidelines for Biomedical and Health Research involving Human Participants when conducting such 
research. 
Research Result Storage and Data Archiving

Early identification of responsibilities for data and sample archiving and destruction, along with 
establishing appropriate methods, is crucial in all research. SRU researchers must prioritize meticulous 
data processing. Research partnership agreements should include terms outlining necessary research 
arrangements. Researchers must maintain detailed and accurate records of all procedures, 
permissions, data collected, and conclusions drawn. This ensures a sound research approach and 
facilitates responses to inquiries about the study's methodology and results. Properly maintained 
notebooks can serve as evidence for intellectual property claims. Data should be stored to allow for 
comprehensive retrospective audits. Backup plans and secure data storage are essential. Original files 
and images must be backed up, especially when modifying existing data or photos for quality 
improvement. When editing data or photographs, both the original and modified versions should be 
retained. Avoid simplifying or manipulating im ages. Confidentiality is particularly important when 
financial advantages are possible. A reliable system for storing and retrieving research data is critical. 
Primary research data must be protected to ensure its continued usability. Researchers must obta in 
permission from the Registrar via the department head before removing any data. The need to 
preserve data sources persists after publication. All raw data should be recorded and stored in 
numbered, permanently bound laboratory notebooks or a dedicated e lectronic notebook. A cross -
index should be the primary record, with all supplementary materials (such as surveys, chart

recordings, autoradiographs, and machine outputs) stored in separate ring binders or folders. Data 
should be recorded in notebooks as soon as practically possible after collection, uniquely identified by 
the date of record and/or collection. Supervisors should regularly check and "sign off" on researchers' 
notebooks to ensure comprehensive data documentation. Regular backups of computer data should 
be made and stored securely yet accessibly, such as on a disc. When feasible, a hard copy of important 
information should be created. Copies of necessary software, especially the version used for electronic 
data processing, must be kept with the raw data. 
Confidentiality in Research and Consultancy 
Principal Investigators and other researchers may handle proprietary or restricted data, materials, 
software, or technology from sponsors or other entities during their work. Sponsors or third parties 
(e.g., firms or government bodies) may require researchers to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA), 
Confidential Disclosure Agreement (CDA), Proprietary Information Agreement (PIA), or Confidentiality 
Agreement. Recipients of confidential technical information (such as proprietary technology, trade 
secrets, or source code) are responsible for complying with export regulations. An export license may 
be necessary if the data is to be sent outside India or shared with a foreign

national; SRU researchers 
are advised to verify this well in advance of such activities. It is important to note that export-regulated 
technology does not include non-technical information with disclosure restrictions, such as sensitive 
financial information, company information, clinical trial/human subjects’ data, or demographic 
information. 
Various university agreements between SRU and sponsors or third parties may include confidentiality 
clauses. Examples include purchases and loans of hardware and software, intellectual property 
licensing, data sharing, and material transfer agreements. SRU 's R&D Cell will be involved in these 
institutional agreements and will negotiate terms aligned with university principles. The R&D Cell has 
the sole authority to sign on behalf of SRU and bind the university to the terms of any negotiated 
institutional agreements. Individual researchers may be asked to sign such agreements by sponsors 
or third parties in connection with clinical trials or potential joint research efforts where all parties 
have a vested interest. In these cases, the NDA is between the indiv idual and the sponsor or third 
party. To avoid associating the signature with SRU, the researcher must sign as an individual. Individual 
researchers intending to sign on their own behalf should seek guidance from the Office of the Dean 
(Research and Rankin g), as

sponsor or third -party NDAs often contain terms that conflict with SRU 
research policy. 
Collaborations and Funded Research 
Collaboration with External Research Peers 
To maximize research output and societal impact through complementary resources, SRU actively 
encourages collaboration with peers. Institutions within India and from other countries can 
collaborate. Any collaboration conducted through a department or school must have clear parameters 
defined in an MOU and/or research collaboration agreement. Scholars can utilize existing Memoranda 
of Understanding (MoUs) or propose new ones to facilitate their research. Scholars are free to conduct 
research at multiple institutions that promote teamwork. 
Funded Research 
SRU's research endeavors are supported by grants and contracts from external funding agencies, 
including state, national, and international governments, as well as industry collaborations, 
consultancy projects, shared consultancy projects, and joint ventur es between institutional groups. 
Research funding is significant as it is peer-reviewed and competitive, indicating the quality of faculty 
research. Scholars are advised to apply for research funding in collaboration with their supervisors 
and external researchers. 
Openness in Research 
The institute recognizes researchers' responsibility to protect their academic and intellectual property 
rights (IPR) but encourages them to make their work as accessible as possible to colleagues and the 
public. Research findings should not be disseminated solely for the promotion of the researcher, the 
institution, or the sponsor. After publication, the author is responsible for making the underlying data

and materials available to other researchers who contact the institute. However, the use of this 
information and materials, as well as the Intellectual Property Rights associated with any publications, 
must comply with all applicable ethical clearances and consents. Guidelines for accessing the institute 
via public transportation are detailed elsewhere. Publication of research findings may be delayed for 
a reasonable period due to intellectual property concerns. Publication delays exceeding three months 
should be avoided. Researchers should exercise caution when publicly sharing preliminary or 
unpublished findings or work that has not undergone peer review. Avoid using email to communicate 
details about pending patent applications. When available, researchers must adhere to the standards 
set by the institute’s sponsoring scientific, scholarly, and other relevant professional organizations. 
Every researcher at SRU should be particularly mindful of health and safety standards and  data 
protection regulations during all research-related activities. 
II. Plagiarism and Abating Plagiarism 
Plagiarism Policy 
Research excellence in the areas of Science and Technology, the Humanities, and Social 
Responsibilities is a goal at university. We demonstrate our dedication to interdisciplinary study by 
continuing to conduct both applied and fundamental studies of lasting

significance. By adhering to the 
strictest scholarly norms, University encourages study across all its primary and interdisciplinary fields. 
Data recording, analysis, and utilization are emphasized. Students at University are encouraged to 
engage in cri tical thinking. Advancing scientific understanding for future generations requires going 
beyond what is taught in schools and what is published in academic journals. The institution's 
philosophy is predicated on the idea that creating research methods to e xpand knowledge and 
developing the full person is essential to fostering a culture of research. SRU will take necessary steps 
to adapt the best practices and protocols to promote research integrity among its students through 
all measures. 
The University acknowledges that the free exchange of ideas is essential to academic endeavours, as 
it is often only through discussion with others that one can completely process information or 
crystallize an elusive concept. Consequently, students are commonly motivated to engage in dialogues 
with their teachers and peers regarding their courses, research, and even homework. These types of 
discussions and debates represent, in some respects, the essence of academic life. Nonetheless, it is 
essential for a ll academics to explicitly acknowledge when they have relied on or incorporated the 
work of others. 
Plagiarism

definition 
According to SR University, plagiarism is "to offer work or ideas from another source as one's own, 
with or without authorization of the source author(s), directly by verbatim copying or by usage of any 
AI software" (i.e., with or without permission from the original author). In certain cases, authorization 
might be provided for the usage of other sources through written permission may not be considered 
as plagiarism. 
Self-plagiarism, a form of plagiarism, can also be committed by reusing one's own work which is 
published in a source without proper citation to that source. It is considered plagiarism in educational 
content to use someone else's idea or phrase without properly attributi ng the source of the work. It 
makes no difference if the source is an accomplished writer, another pupil, a web page without 
distinguished authorship, a website that sells research papers, or anyone else as well, whether done 
knowingly or unintentionally, claiming credit for someone else's work is considered as a form of 
academic theft and is despicable in all educational environments. 
An act of "plagiarism" is any use of words or concepts from another writer without giving proper credit 
to them. Plagiarism is the unacknowledged use of another author's words, ideas, or structure in one's 
own work, whether those words, ideas, or structure are published or not.  
Misrepresentation: Research and publications are misunderstood; there has been fabrication and 
distortion of research material published in book chapters, journals, and conference proceedings.

Redundant submission: Not getting permission from your teacher before submitting work that has 
been submitted in whole or in significant part for another class or course that is already used for 
academic purposes. 
Forms of plagiarism 
Verbatim: Quotations must be marked with quotation marks or indentation and fully cited. The reader 
must know which parts are your own and which are borrowed. 
Cut and paste: This type is defined when a person copies and paste the content from sources including 
internet, the list of sources must include references to Internet -derived information. Since Internet 
content is less likely to have been peer-reviewed, it should be carefully assessed. 
Paraphrasing: Without proper citation, replicating someone else's work by altering a few words and 
rearranging the sequence in which they appear or by closely following the framework of their 
argument to develop another related content. 
Collusion: This can include things like working together on a project without permission, failing to 
properly credit third -party assistance, or failing to adhere to guidelines for working in groups. You 
should know exactly how much teamwork is allowed and what respon sibilities fall solely on one's 
shoulders. 
Inaccurate citation: Always use the standard format for citations in the area, one works in. Author 
should cite the sources not only at the end of the

paper (in a bibliography), but also within the text 
itself (in a footnote). Also, one should not include books, articles, or w ebsites in the bibliography or 
references that you did not consult. 
Failure to acknowledge assistance: One should provide proper credit to any source who helped you 
while creating your work, whether they are classmates, lab assistants, or anyone else.  
Auto-plagiarism (Identical submission): One must not develop or submit an assessment related work 
that is already submitted either in partial or full, for a course or for any other qualification, from this 
university or other, electronically, or manually.

Plagiarism Identification and Repercussion 
Plagiarism is a serious academic offense, and SRU strongly advises its scholars to avoid it. Scholars 
submitting academic documents must carefully evaluate their content to prevent any form of 
plagiarism. All academic documents submitted by scholars during  their studies, including theses, 
research papers, conference papers, and related materials, will be checked for plagiarism. 
Procedure for Plagiarism Check for Masters/ PhD Thesis    
Scholars who

meet the University's PhD thesis submission requirements are eligible to submit. The 
Scholar and Supervisor should declare that the material is their original work and plagiarism -free, as 
per PhD requirements. SRU strongly discourage plagiarised content submission in any form.  
Supervisor may also verify that there is no copyright violation in the document. 
Supervisor of the scholar should verify that there is no plagiarism in the document and recommend it 
to the research office. 
Submission of the thesis in the final version is the responsibility of the supervisor.   
Once the file is submitted, the research office will verify the same using standard plagiarism software 
(Turnitin/ iThenticate) and inform the supervisor with the outcome and level of similarity present. 
Dean (Research and Ranking) shall evaluate the report and act as follows. 
In the case of Level 0, the thesis will be passed on as per the regulations.  
In the case of Level 1, the scholar/ student will be asked to revise and resubmit within 30 days. 
In the case of Level 2 and 3 – Necessary action will be taken and will recommend penalty as per 
regulations and UGC norms. 
Procedure for Plagiarism Check (Articles and book chapters) 
Any author who wishes to submit the paper can submit the pdf version of the final paper to the

book chapter/ book content/ 
journal article or an unfinished manuscript.

supervisor is responsible.  
Penalties 
Only after all possible appeals have been exhausted and the individual in question has been given 
enough time to defend himself or herself in a fair or transparent manner may disciplinary measures 
be taken against an individual enrolled in a master’s or Re search program, or a researcher, staff 
member, or staff member of the University, for academic misconduct. Any benefit of the doubt should 
be issued in favour of the student/scholar/ staff. 
Suggested penalties for integrity issues  
Academic Integrity Committee (AIC) shall impose a penalty considering the severity of the Plagiarism.  
Level 0: Similarities up to 10% - Single source plagiarism, if less than 1% no penalty.

Level 1: Similarities above 10% to 20% - Scholar/ student will be asked to revise and resubmit within 
30 days, S/he will be provided with only one chance to revise.  
Level 2:  Similarities above 20% - Punishment as per the regulations will be initiated, and the 
student/scholar will be barred for one year from submitting any document for academic purposes. 
Such a student/scholar may also be asked to forgo registration of the program. 
Penalty on repeated offense: Such a student will face the consequences for the next level of plagiarism 
committed. In the event of severe plagiarism, the corresponding penalties must be enforced.

prima facie shown after the degree (Masters/PhD) or credit (in appraisal) has been issued, the 
University will invalidate the degree or credit. The degree/award will be put on hold until the 
beneficiary can explain the reported misbehaviour.  
The AIC recommends and the Vice-Chancellor approves the action as mentioned below. 
The thesis will be withdrawn from all the repositories it was submitted. 
A show cause notice will be issued to the scholar and the supervisor. 
Disciplinary action may be initiated against the supervisor within the rules of the university.  
If the student does not cooperate, employer, if any will be contacted and informed

about the outcome 
of the action duly. 
University is entitled to cancel the degree/award/credit given for the course as per the ordinances.

Level 1: Similarities above 10% to 20%- Paper should be withdrawn immediately.

strongly urge its faculties and scholars to acknowledge all sources and support they
